title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 167 (Right of third person claiming goods bailed)

content.overview: Section 167 provides that if a person, other than the bailor, claims goods bailed, he may apply to the Court to stop the delivery of the goods to the bailor, and to decide the title to the goods.
content.glance: A third person claiming goods bailed may apply to the Court to stop delivery to the bailor and to decide title.
content.study: If a person, other than the bailor, claims goods bailed, he may apply to the Court to stop the delivery of the goods to the bailor, and to decide the title to the goods. Current-law framing: provides a court mechanism for competing claims to goods in the bailee's possession.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If a person, other than the bailor, claims goods bailed, he may apply to the Court to stop the delivery of the goods to the bailor, and to decide the title to the goods.

examples.title: Third-party claim
examples.body: A third person claims title to goods in the bailee's possession and applies to Court under Section 167 to stop delivery to the bailor.

hypotheticals.question: A third person claims the goods bailed. What remedy does Section 167 provide?
hypotheticals.analysis: He may apply to the Court to stop delivery to the bailor and to decide the title.
